Do you think a million-dollar term life insurance policy sounds like too much insurance?

As a Certified Financial Planner, I see underinsured people every day.

A million-dollar term life insurance policy might actually be the minimum coverage needed for the typical middle-class household, but it’s affordable.

That might sound like an exaggeration, but if you crunch the numbers – just as we’ll be doing a little bit – you’ll realize that a million-dollar policy might be just what you need.

The good news is term life insurance isn’t nearly as costly as most people think.

What makes term life insurance even better is that larger policies cost less on a per thousand basis than smaller policies do. You may find the premium on a $1 million policy is only a little bit higher than it is for $500,000.

Sources indicate that probably, but let’s find out. A general rule of thumb is that you should get 10x your income as baseline coverage for life insurance.

If you’re young, that may be low because you may want to provide your family with enough to replace your income for 15 years or more.

Today, $1 million has become the new baseline for life insurance by a primary breadwinner. Anything less could leave your family financially impaired.

Here’s a list of all the different obligations you may want to have life insurance cover in the unfortunate event you pass away early.

Now that you have an idea of these obligations, let’s punch them into this life insurance calculator to find out if you need a million-dollar policy.

Industry observers note that according to Policy Genius, the average cost for a 20-year $1 million term life insurance policy for a 35-year-old male is $53 per month. However, your rate will vary according to the following factors.

Sources indicate that the best, and easiest place to start is online. I recommend having two or three insurers compete for your business to make sure you get the best rate and coverage. To see how cheap term life can be, choose your state from the map above to be matched with top life insurance providers instantly.

Let’s look at the individual components that can promptly add up to over a million-dollar policy.

This is where things can get a bit intimidating. Even if you earn a modest income, you may need close to $1 million to replace that income after your death in order to provide for your family’s basic living expenses.

The conventional wisdom in the insurance industry is that you should maintain a life insurance policy equal to between 10 times and 20 times your annual income. So if you earn around $50K per year, that would mean policy coverage between $500K and $1 million.

The complication today is that with interest rates being as low as they are that might not be enough either.

For example, if you have a $1 million policy that could be invested at 5% per year, your family could live on the interest earned – which conveniently comes to $50,000 per year – for the next 20 years.

That would still leave the original $1 million intact to cover other expenses. But with today’s microscopic interest rates, there’s no way to get a guaranteed return of 5% on your money, certainly not for 15 or 20 years.

In a recent development, also, keep in mind that most insurance companies have a maximum multiplier you can apply to your income for life insurance coverage. For example, it wouldn’t make much sense for a 22-year-old making $27,000 per year to get a $2 million life insurance. Or a 65-year-old that is retired to secure a $3 million dollar policy.

The table below is approximately how much you’re allowed to multiply your income based on your age and income:.

Using the table above as a guide, a 35-year-old making $150,000 per year would be capped at taking out a $4.5 million term policy ($150,000 x 30 = $4,500,000).

Here we start with the basics – wrapping up your final affairs.

It has been revealed that this will include funeral costs and any lingering medical costs. A reasonable estimate for a typical funeral is around $20,000.

Recent findings suggest that crazy, right? You can get burial insurance to cover only the most basic of final expenses.

Debt burdens are high in the US, and debt can be especially crushing on remaining family members. Many life insurance customers make sure they can pay off most of their debt with the policy.

Recent findings suggest that medical costs are a serious variable. Even if you have excellent health insurance, there are likely to be unpaid medical bills lingering after your death. This has to do with copayments, deductibles, and coinsurance provisions.

Recent findings suggest that collectively, they can add up to many thousands of dollars. But where things get really complicated is if you die of a terminal illness.

For example, if you are stricken by an illness that lasts for several years, you could incur a number of expenses that are not covered by insurance. This may include the cost of personal care and even experimental treatments.

Sources indicate that A home may be a large asset, but it’s also often a homeowner’s largest debt. The average mortgage balance in the US is roughly $236,443 according to Experian data. So you could easily use a life insurance policy to pay off that debt and relieve your loved ones of a monthly mortgage payment.

Industry observers note that credit card debt and other personal debt are some of the most expensive obligations carrying rates upward of 20% in some cases. Make sure you have enough to cover this very expensive debt.

Below is a sampling of major expenses your family is likely to incur, either on an annual basis or at some point after your death.

It has been revealed that tuition costs continue to skyrocket. The Department of Education suggests that four-year public college tuition has been rising an average of 5% per year, far exceeding the rate of inflation. If you have one child who attends an in-state public school, a second at an out-of-state public school, and a third in a private university, the total expenditure will reach $416,560.

Vehicles and other forms of transportation represent another large sum. Unfortunately, with increasing electronics and safety features, the average cost of a new car continues to grow.

Recent findings suggest that if your family relies on your work for healthcare, take notice. According to eHealth.com, the average health insurance premium for a family is $22,221. That’s a shade under $2,000 per month in additional cost. This cost will only rise, and the need could last for years.

So far, we’ve been describing the financial obligations likely to affect a typical household.But there may be certain situations that will produce obligations that are less obvious.

For example, if you’re a business owner, there may be debts or other financial obligations that will need to be paid upon your death.

Even though no one in your family may be qualified or interested in taking over your business, the payoff of those obligations may be completely necessary to enable the sale of the business.

Another possibility is that you’re a real estate investor.

If your properties are heavily indebted, extra insurance proceeds may be necessary either to carry the properties until they’re sold, or even to pay off existing indebtedness to free up cash flow for income.

You may even need additional funds if you are taking care of an extended family member, like an aging parent.

These are just some of the many possibilities of expenses that will need to be covered by insurance proceeds.

Before we move on to specific life insurance quotes, let’s first consider the factors that affect term life insurance premiums.

Recent findings suggest that this is typically the single most important premium factor. The older you are, the more likely you are to die within the term of the policy.

This is a close second and why it’s so vital to apply for a policy as early in life as possible. Premiums on life insurances rates literally increase by each year.

In a recent development, if you have any health conditions that may affect mortality, such as diabetes or hypertension, your premiums will be higher. This is another compelling reason to apply while you are young and in good health.

It’s not that policies are not available to people with health conditions, it’s just that they’re less expensive if you don’t have any.

A 10-year term policy will have a lower premium than a 20-year term policy, which will be lower than a 30-year term. The shorter the term, the less likely it is the insurance tech giant will have to pay a claim before it expires.

Size of the policy matters, but not the way you might think. Yes, a $1 million policy will cost more than a $500,000 policy. But it won’t cost twice as much.

The larger the policy, the lower the per-thousand cost will be.

When the size of the death benefit is considered, the larger policy will always be more cost-effective.

In a recent development, for example, certain occupations are more hazardous than others (think policeman versus librarian). Deep-sea diving is higher risk than golf. And smoking is the one activity guaranteed to raise your premiums substantially.

With this information in mind, let’s take a look at whether you should consider a $1 million whole life policy instead.

Any discussion on life insurance should include a comparison of whole life and term life insurance coverage. After all, both products can be immensely valuable in the right situation, yet one product (whole life) costs considerably more than the other.

Most of the time, the debate is settled in favor of term life insurance based on cost alone.

A whole life insurance policy can easily cost 10x the same amount of coverage you can get with a term policy.

It has been revealed that with that being said, whole life insurance and other investment-type life insurance coverage can be valuable in terms of the cash value you can build up over time. Whole life insurance also offers a fixed benefit amount for your heirs that will last for your entire life, yet the cost of your premiums are guaranteed to stay the same.

The cash value of a whole life insurance policy also grows on a tax-deferred basis, and you can borrow against this amount if you need a loan. Further, many whole life policies from reputable providers also pay out dividends during good years, which can be substantial.

The problem with whole life and other similar policies like universal life is the fact that premiums can be exorbitant for the amount of coverage you might need.

A couple with young children provides a good example since they might need a $1 million dollar policy or more to provide income protection for their working years and have money left for college tuition and other expenses.

With young families, expenses are already high.

This includes costs for food for a family, childcare, heavy use of health care, and the seemingly endless demand for clothing, furniture, and even entertainment as the children grow.

As you can see from the cost comparison below from State Farm, there’s not enough room in the typical family budget to afford the type of life insurance that’s needed.

Points for Business/First Class.

Sources indicate that picture this: you settle into a Lufthansa Boeing 747-8 business class seat on the upper deck, somewhere over the Atlantic, a glass of Champagne in hand, your fully flat bed already made up behind you. No carrier-imposed fees eating into your redemption. Just the experience. That's the moment the FI community lives for. Not the luxury itself — though Lufthansa's business class product is genuinely exceptional — but the *math*. The realization that the loyalty system has a pricing gap so wide you could fly a 747 through it. Here's what the numbers actually mean. At the low end, a $4,000 business class ticket redeemed for 63,000 points works out to **6.3 cents per point (CPP)**. At the high end — peak travel season, last-minute pricing, transatlantic demand — that same seat hits $8,000 in cash, which means your LifeMiles are delivering **12.7 cents per point**. For context, most travel rewards experts consider 1–2 CPP a baseline for points value. You're achieving 6 to 12 times that baseline. The reason this feels like a genuine inefficiency rather than just a deal: Avianca LifeMiles prices Star Alliance awards on a **fixed award chart** that doesn't fluctuate with cash fare demand. When airlines raise transatlantic business class fares during summer holidays or major events, your points cost stays exactly the same. The gap between what the market charges and what LifeMiles charges simply grows wider. And then there's the no-fuel-surcharge policy — the detail that separates LifeMiles from competitors like British Airways Avios, which can pile $600+ in carrier surcharges onto a single redemption. With LifeMiles, you pay government taxes only, typically $50–$150 for a transatlantic itinerary. That's it. For the ChooseFI community, this redemption represents exactly the kind of asymmetric value that underpins a great travel rewards strategy: use points where cash prices are highest, eliminate fees wherever possible, and fly a product you'd never justify paying full price for — because you didn't have to.

The core insight here is understanding why Avianca LifeMiles prices Star Alliance awards so aggressively — and then understanding how to get points into the program quickly enough to actually use them.

Avianca is a Star Alliance member, which means it has reciprocal award booking agreements with every other Star Alliance carrier — United, Lufthansa, Swiss, ANA, EVA Air, Singapore Airlines, and more. Like all alliance programs, LifeMiles can sell award seats on partner airlines. The pricing is set by Avianca's own award chart, not by Lufthansa's chart or United's chart.

Recent findings suggest that this is the pricing inefficiency. Lufthansa's own frequent flyer program (Miles & More) charges over 100,000 miles for the same transatlantic business class route and layers on fuel surcharges. United MileagePlus charges 70,000–88,000 miles for the same seat. Avianca LifeMiles charges 63,000 miles with zero carrier surcharges. Same seat. Same plane. Wildly different cost.

Avianca keeps rates competitive because they want their program to be attractive to non-Avianca flyers — it's a revenue play. And because their route network is South America-focused, they've built a powerful award program that earns loyalty from customers who may never set foot on an Avianca plane.

Many programs claim no surcharges, then quietly pass through "carrier-imposed fees" that look indistinguishable from surcharges. LifeMiles is one of the genuine exceptions. On partner award bookings — including Lufthansa, Swiss, and other carriers that traditionally levy heavy surcharges — LifeMiles charges only government taxes. For a JFK–FRA business class award, expect to pay roughly $50–$150 out of pocket. That's the full cash outlay.

According to recent reports, after booking, you'll receive a confirmation email with a PNR (record locator). Save this confirmation and check it once more 72 hours before departure.

It has been revealed that avianca LifeMiles uses a distance-based award chart for Star Alliance partner flights, and their chart is consistently 15-40% cheaper than competing programs for the same seats. The reason is strategic: Avianca wants to attract members to its loyalty program, and aggressive pricing on aspirational redemptions is how they compete with larger alliances. For you, this means the exact same Lufthansa First Class seat or ANA business class seat costs significantly fewer points when booked through LifeMiles versus through United MileagePlus or the carrier directly. The catch is that LifeMiles availability depends on the operating carrier releasing award space to partners, so you still need to search on the carrier or United.com before transferring.

Mailchimp SMS Marketing Review – One List for Texts & Emails, but Credits Expire Monthly

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (948 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Moneycrashers

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that add Mailchimp SMS Marketing if you already email customers from Mailchimp and want texts in the same audience and automation flows.
  • Mailchimp started in Atlanta in 2001 as an email service for small businesses, and Intuit bought it in 2021.
  • Texting needs a paid Mailchimp email plan, Essentials or higher, and several features below need Standard or Premium.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that add Mailchimp SMS Marketing if you already email customers from Mailchimp and want texts in the same audience and automation flows. It starts at $20 a month for 1,000 U.S. credits, and unused credits expire every month, so a store that sells mostly by text should choose a service built for texting.

Mailchimp started in Atlanta in 2001 as an email service for small businesses, and Intuit bought it in 2021. Its texting add-on sends to the U.S., Canada, Australia, and more than 30 European countries, and every business has to apply and be approved before its first text goes out.

Texting needs a paid Mailchimp email plan, Essentials or higher, and several features below need Standard or Premium.

A text written with plain letters, numbers, and common symbols holds 160 characters, and one with an emoji or another special character holds 70. A longer text splits into parts of 153 or 67 characters, and each part uses its own credits. Your organization name opens every text by default, since some carriers require it, and it counts toward the limit along with spaces, emojis, and opt-out instructions.

In a recent development, on the Standard and Premium plans, programs in the U.S. and Canada can also send picture messages, called MMS. Each carries one JPEG, PNG, or GIF and up to 1,600 characters, and costs 3 credits in the U.S. and 5 in Canada. Those plans also get branded short links, which shorten your links under a subdomain you choose. On any blueprint, the builder can shorten and track links, add merge tags that personalize each text, and insert a discount code from a Shopify, WooCommerce, BigCommerce, Magento, PrestaShop, or Lightspeed store.

You can add a Send SMS step to the same automation flows that send your emails. Mailchimp’s prebuilt flows include one for abandoned carts, which texts a shopper once per cart left behind. A text a flow triggers during quiet hours, the late-night and early-morning window when marketing texts are held, waits until they end. On the Essentials proposal, a flow holds no more than four steps.

In a recent development, each country needs its own registered sending number, and texts reach only contacts in the countries you’ve registered. A text uses 1 credit in the U.S., 3 in Canada, 5 in the U.K., and 12 in Germany. U.S. businesses on Standard or higher can also apply for a short code, a 5- or 6-digit number built for large audiences. It costs extra, and carriers take 8 to 12 weeks to review the application.

Replies land in Mailchimp’s Inbox, and every answer you send uses credits. You can reply to a contact three times in 7 days, and the 7-day window restarts each time they text you again. That covers a question about an order, not ongoing customer service by text. On a two-way number, replies of STOP or HELP get automatic answers that use no credits.

In a recent development, credits come in monthly blocks. On Mailchimp’s U.S. pricing page, 1,000 credits cost $20 a month, 2,500 cost $25, 5,000 cost $45, and 10,000 cost $90, with blocks up to 450,000 for $2,500. By our math, a plain U.S. text costs 2 cents at the smallest block and 0.9 cents at 5,000 or 10,000. Mailchimp’s 14-day free trial of its email looks doesn’t cover texting, and the Free blueprint can’t add it.

Your block renews with your email proposal each month, and unused credits expire when the next billing cycle starts. A refill bought mid-month costs full price, while a change to your monthly block takes effect at the next cycle. You pay nothing until your application is approved, the first month is prorated, and refunds come only for a system malfunction or an account closed without cause.

Sources indicate that email consent doesn’t cover texts, so each contact has to opt in to SMS through Mailchimp’s signup landing page or an SMS phone field added to your other signup forms. Mailchimp’s own SMS signup forms record the date and time each contact was asked and agreed, and importing a list means confirming that every contact gave explicit SMS consent.

Carriers bar texts about sex, hate, firearms, tobacco, cannabis, gambling, and political campaigns, and they allow alcohol only in programs that verify age. Among financial services, high-interest loans and debt collection are barred too, and breaking the rules can get an account suspended. In the U.S., carriers cap how fast texts go out by a score they give each business, from 75 a minute to AT&T customers at the entry tier to 4,500 at the top. Texts over the cap wait in a queue. Every U.S. account is registered with carriers automatically, and an upgrade called standard vetting may speed up sending. It comes with a block of 5,000 or more credits or with the Premium proposal.

Mailchimp SMS Marketing works best as an extension of email you already send from Mailchimp. Texts reach the same audience through the same segments and flows, the compliance work runs in the background, and a small U.S. program costs $20 to $25 a month.

Mailchimp Review – Easy to Use, Pricey Once Your List Grows

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (959 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Moneycrashers

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, mailchimp lets a small business send polished marketing email without a designer or a developer.
  • Recent findings suggest that ben Chestnut and Dan Kurzius started Mailchimp in Atlanta in 2001 as a small-business email service on the side of their web design agency, and the firm is still based there.
  • Recent findings suggest that mailchimp sells four looks: Free, Essentials, Standard, and Premium.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, mailchimp lets a small business send polished marketing email without a designer or a developer. Its templates and drag-and-drop editor handle the design, and its integrations bring in your customers and their purchases from the store or website you already run. The trade-off is a price that rises with each tier of contacts you store.

Recent findings suggest that ben Chestnut and Dan Kurzius started Mailchimp in Atlanta in 2001 as a small-business email service on the side of their web design agency, and the firm is still based there. Intuit, the maker of QuickBooks and TurboTax, bought it in 2021, and Mailchimp indicates it now has more than 11 million owners.

Recent findings suggest that mailchimp sells four looks: Free, Essentials, Standard, and Premium. All four share the same email builder, sign-up forms, landing pages, and directory of more than 300 integrations, and the paid tiers add automation, testing, and reporting.

According to recent reports, the drag-and-drop builder starts from more than 130 templates on paid intends, while the Free strategy gets a limited selection and puts Mailchimp’s branding on every email. Paid plans also let you schedule sends.

Standard and Premium add generative AI, still in beta, that drafts and rewrites copy in the editor. They also let you send templates you code yourself in HTML and use dynamic content, which changes parts of an email for each reader.

It has been revealed that automation flows send emails on their own when a contact does something, such as joining your list or leaving items in a cart. Essentials limits each flow to four steps. Standard and Premium allow up to 200 flows, with branches that send contacts down different paths and more than one starting point.

According to recent reports, A/B testing comes with every paid plan. It tries up to three versions of a subject line, sender name, content, or send time on part of your list, then can send the winner to the rest automatically. Standard and Premium add multivariate testing, which compares up to eight versions at once, plus send-time optimization, which picks a send time from your list’s past clicks.

Every plan can build sign-up forms and landing pages, and a landing page can sit on a Mailchimp address or on a domain you connect. The integrations directory lists more than 300 apps, including Shopify, WooCommerce, Square, Wix, Squarespace, Stripe, Canva, Zapier, and QuickBooks Online. A connected store such as Shopify syncs customers and purchases into Mailchimp, which uses them for product recommendations and abandoned-cart emails.

Every initiative includes basic campaign reports. Standard and Premium add custom reports, advanced segmentation, and predictive segments that group customers by predicted lifetime value or likelihood to buy.

In a recent development, each paid strategy is priced by contact tier, a band such as 2,501 to 5,000 contacts, and the top of your tier is your contact limit. Your monthly send limit is a multiple of it. Here’s where each plan starts:.

The price rises promptly. Standard costs $45 a month at 1,500 contacts, $100 at 5,000, and $135 at 10,000, almost seven times its starting price. Essentials runs $26.50, $75, and $110 at the same sizes.

It has been revealed that discounts are narrow. A new customer who skips the trial and buys a plan at 10,000 or more contacts gets 15% off the first 12 months, and nonprofits and charities get 15% off on request. Essentials and Standard come with a 14-day free trial that bills the plan’s price when it ends unless you cancel. If you send only a few times a year, Pay As You Go sells email credits with Essentials’ features instead of a subscription, though the credits expire after 12 months.

Text messaging costs extra as well, since Mailchimp SMS Marketing is a paid add-on that needs Mailchimp’s approval of your application first.

For a substantial list you email a few times a month, look at Brevo, which prices its intends by the emails you send rather than the contacts you keep. Its Standard blueprint, which also includes automation and A/B testing, costs $69 a month for 20,000 emails, enough to reach 10,000 contacts twice. Mailchimp’s Standard plan costs $135 a month at 10,000 contacts, though it allows 120,000 sends and five seats to Brevo’s one. Brevo’s free plan holds up to 100,000 contacts and sends up to 300 emails a day.

Essentials and Standard come with 24/7 email and chat support, and Premium adds priority support and phone calls, which are in English only. The Free proposal gets email support for its first 30 days only. Standard includes one hour-long onboarding session in your first 90 days, and Premium includes up to four.

In a recent development, reviews depend on where you look. Mailchimp averages 4.3 out of 5 from about 13,000 reviews on G2, a software review site, but 2.5 out of 5 from about 1,600 on Trustpilot.

Recent findings suggest that mailchimp makes it easy for a small business to start an email list that works with the store or website it already runs, and Standard is its best plan while the list is small. At 500 contacts, $20 a month buys automation flows, multivariate testing, generative AI, and an onboarding session.

H&R Block Review – Free for Simple Returns, With Tax Pros Online or in Person

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1298 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Moneycrashers

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, file with H&R Block if your return fits Free Online, which takes retirement, Social Security, and unemployment income with a free state return, or if you want tax pros to answer questions or sign your return.
  • According to recent reports, doing your own taxes costs less than paying a preparer, but it leaves you alone with any form you don’t understand.
  • According to recent reports, brothers Henry and Richard Bloch founded H&R Block in 1955 in Kansas City, Missouri, where it’s still based.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, file with H&R Block if your return fits Free Online, which takes retirement, Social Security, and unemployment income with a free state return, or if you want tax pros to answer questions or sign your return. If you need a paid tier but no help, file with a free program instead.

According to recent reports, doing your own taxes costs less than paying a preparer, but it leaves you alone with any form you don’t understand. H&R Block offers several kinds of help in between. Its online software files simple returns free, and its paid tiers include live tax pros who answer questions. For an added fee, a pro will check and file your return, or prepare it for you, online or in an office.

According to recent reports, brothers Henry and Richard Bloch founded H&R Block in 1955 in Kansas City, Missouri, where it’s still based. It has about 11,000 tax offices worldwide, with locations in every state, and nearly 60,000 tax pros. In its fiscal year ended June 30, 2026, its pros prepared 11.3 million U.S. returns, and customers prepared 3.6 million returns themselves in its paid online tiers.

H&R Block sorts its online software into four tiers by the forms a return needs, and the tier sets the price. Any return can start in Free Online, and H&R Block notes it moves you to a paid tier only when your situation requires one.

Free Online charges nothing for federal or state returns. It takes W-2 wages, unemployment benefits, retirement initiative distributions, Social Security, and up to $1,500 of interest and dividends. It also claims the Earned Income Tax Credit, the Child Tax Credit, education credits, and the student loan interest deduction. Its form list for 2025 returns included Schedule 1-A, which claims the new deductions for tips, overtime, car loan interest, and seniors.

In a recent development, it can’t itemize deductions, and it leaves out freelance or business income, rental income, stock sales, foreign income, and health savings accounts (HSAs). H&R Block notes about 52% of filers qualify, without saying how it counts them. A Federal Trade Commission (FTC) order requires its ads for free filing to give that share or say that most filers don’t qualify. Since the 2026 season, the same order has required H&R Block to return a filer who upgrades and then moves back down to the point they’d reached before upgrading, instead of starting them over.

Each paid tier adds forms the one before it lacks, and each charges $49 for every state return on top of its federal price.

Deluxe, Premium, and Self-Employed include unlimited help at no extra charge, and Free Online includes none. AI Tax Assist, H&R Block’s chatbot, answers tax questions at any hour and any step, and live tax pros take the ones you’d rather ask a person. The help is for your questions. For a pro to check, sign, and file your return, you add Tax Pro Review, which costs extra.

Tax Pro Review puts a tax pro on your return without an office visit. When you finish, the pro checks your return and documents for errors and missed deductions or credits, asks for anything more they need, and signs and e-files the return once you approve any changes. H&R Block says the review usually takes up to three days after you send your documents, though timing varies with a return’s complexity and in peak weeks. It adds $75 to Free Online, $65 to Deluxe, and $95 to Premium or Self-Employed.

According to recent reports, A pro can also prepare the whole return, starting at $99 plus a state fee. You can meet one at an H&R Block office, drop your documents off at one, or work with a pro from home through its MyBlock app.

It has been revealed that moving from another program takes an upload of last year’s Form 1040, or H&R Block will transfer the return for you. It notes a return from TurboTax or another tax prep service comes over in as little as two minutes. A federal refund deposited to Spruce, H&R Block’s banking app, can arrive up to five days early.

It has been revealed that the prices in this review are what H&R Block charges for 2025 returns. It usually opens the next season’s online software in November, and its prices for 2026 returns may differ.

It has been revealed that at those prices, a homeowner who itemizes and files one state return pays $114 in Deluxe, $65 plus $49 for the state, or $179 with Tax Pro Review. A freelancer who deducts business expenses needs Self-Employed, which comes to $179 with one state, or $274 with Tax Pro Review. Free Online with Tax Pro Review costs $75, state return included.

Each paid tier’s price includes its help, whether you use it or not. For a filer who won’t use the help, Cash App Taxes charges $0 for federal and state returns, freelance income and stock sales included, though it gives no tax advice. If you’re choosing between H&R Block and TurboTax, price the tier your return needs at both before you start.

It has been revealed that H&R Block’s guarantees depend on who prepared the return. On a return you prepare in its online software, the 100% Accuracy Guarantee reimburses penalties and interest caused by a software error, up to $10,000. On one its tax pro prepares, it reimburses penalties and interest from an H&R Block error, with no cap stated.

It has been revealed that the Maximum Refund Guarantee refunds the software fees if a software error left you a smaller refund or a larger tax bill than you were due, and you can amend the return in the software at no charge. You must claim it during the calendar year the return was prepared. Neither guarantee covers a mistake caused by incomplete or inaccurate information you supplied.

Sources indicate that if the IRS or your state sends a notice about a return you filed online, H&R Block explains it and gives you steps to respond at no extra charge. Someone to represent you at an audit costs extra. Worry-Free Audit Support, which you can buy with any online tier, adds in-person representation by an H&R Block enrolled agent, a tax specialist licensed by the IRS but not an attorney. It pays none of the tax, penalties, or interest you owe, and you have 60 days from the notice to tell H&R Block.

Industry observers note that H&R Block is worth it for two kinds of filers. One has a return that fits Free Online, which files a federal and a state return at no cost for more kinds of income than W-2 wages alone. The other wants a tax pro to ask, to check the return, or to prepare it, online or in an office.

It’s the wrong pick for a return that needs a paid tier but no help, since the tier’s price includes the help either way and a free program costs nothing. Start your return in Free Online and let H&R Block show you which tier your forms need before you pay for one.

It has been revealed that having more than one type of debt is common, and that’s especially true once you graduate from college and start your first “real job.” You may have credit card debt, an auto loan, and a mortgage payment to make once you buy your first home. It’s also common to have other random debts to cover, including student loans.

According to recent reports, if you’re like many who took out loans during college, you will likely be paying them off after you graduate. In fact, 82% of students who borrowed loans expect to be making payments post-graduation, according to a recent College Ave Student Loans survey.

That said, you’ll want to make sure you’re balancing debt repayment with your savings goals along the way.

In a recent development, you’ll also want to make sure you’re paying down debts in the optimal order, or in a way that will help you save the most money on interest as possible while aligning with your goals. Which debts should you pay off first? Here’s a rundown of how to get the best results:.

No matter which types of debt you have, credit card debt should be your first priority. Why? Because credit card debt is likely the most expensive debt you have by far.

Federal Reserve data reveals the average credit card interest rate on accounts assessed interest came in at around 22% as of May 2023, yet your credit card could easily be charging higher rates than the average.

Industry observers note that to save as much money as possible, you should strive to pay as much as you can toward high-interest credit card bills each month. You can also pay down credit card debt faster with the help of a debt consolidation loan or a 0% APR balance transfer credit card.

Sources indicate that other unsecured debts like personal loan debt should come next in the debt payoff pecking order. After all, unsecured debts tend to have higher interest rates than secured debts like auto loans. In fact, the Federal Reserve also reported that the average interest rate on a 24-month personal loan came in at 11.48% as of May 2023, compared to the average rate of 7.81% on a 60-month auto loan.

Ideally, you’ll start paying more toward personal loan debt and other unsecured debts after all credit card debt is entirely paid off, although you should make at least the minimum payment on all your bills throughout the entire process.

According to recent reports, the next debt you’ll want to tackle is your student loans. I suggest focusing on these loans after other unsecured debts, since federal student loans (and many private student loans) come with low fixed interest rates and monthly payments that will not change over time. If you have federal student loans, you may even want to look into income-driven repayment aims.

If you’re hoping to pay down student loans faster or just want to save money on interest, you can also consider refinancing your student loans to get a shorter repayment timeline, a lower monthly payment, or both. Just remember that refinancing federal student loans can mean losing access to income-driven repayment plans and federal protections like deferment and forbearance.

Once you have paid off or substantially paid down all your other debts, you can focus your efforts on secured debts you have like mortgage loans and auto loans. These debts should be dealt with last since they are secured with collateral and tend to offer lower interest rates as a result. For example, you can consider paying more than the minimum on your mortgage, a car loan, or both until they’re paid off completely.

Then again, you may want to pay off debts with extremely low interest rates as slowly as possible to free up more cash flow for living expenses and investments. If you took out a mortgage in January of 2021 when the average interest rate on a 30-year, fixed rate home loan was as low as 2.65%, for example, it makes sense to make the minimum payment on that debt and invest your extra cash instead.

In a recent development, it’s important to make sure you balance debt repayment with other financial considerations. After all, focusing too much on debt repayment early in life can leave you behind when it comes to investing for retirement or saving up for a first home.

While you’ll want to eliminate credit card debt and other high-interest debts as quickly as you can, even if you have to stop saving and investing for a while, you can pay down student loan debt and secured debts at a slower pace while saving and investing for the future along the way.

Sources indicate that finally, make sure you have adequate emergency savings throughout your entire debt payoff journey, or that you begin saving for emergencies as soon as you can. Without a fully funded emergency fund, you can end up relying on credit cards and other loans to get by and ruin your debt payoff progress in the process.

Industry observers note that how much should you save? While most experts recommend having an emergency fund that can cover three to six months of expenses, it’s okay to start small if you have to.

Having more than one type of debt is how it works for most people, especially when you’re young and in the early stages of your career. When it comes to paying it off, however, you’ll want to make sure you have a concrete plan that can help you reduce interest charges and get where you want to be.

Focusing on credit card debt and other unsecured debts first always makes sense, since these debts aren’t secured by an asset and tend to charge much higher interest rates. You can focus on student loans next, followed by other secured debts you have like a home loan or car loan.

In the meantime, make sure you have an adequate emergency fund and invest in it for retirement. After all, debt won’t last forever if you’re serious about repayment, and saving and investing early can help you benefit from compound interest and avoid using credit cards for surprise expenses. Creating a budget to track these factors is your best bet.

If you need help creating one, or simply don’t know where to start, use this budget worksheet as your guide – you’ll reach financial freedom in no time.

  • In a recent development, buy one of the VSP Individual Vision Aims if you get newly introduced glasses or contacts every year from a VSP doctor, since the $150 allowance and $15 exam copay can save more than the premiums cost.
  • Recent findings suggest that retiring or leaving a job usually ends your vision coverage, and then you pay the full price of an exam and new glasses yourself.
  • VSP, a not-for-profit vision benefits manufacturer founded in 1955, is based in Rancho Cordova, California, and sells these plans directly on its own website.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, buy one of the VSP Individual Vision Aims if you get newly introduced glasses or contacts every year from a VSP doctor, since the $150 allowance and $15 exam copay can save more than the premiums cost. If you need only an exam or buy glasses online elsewhere, skip it and pay out of pocket.

Recent findings suggest that retiring or leaving a job usually ends your vision coverage, and then you pay the full price of an exam and new glasses yourself. VSP created its individual plans for people without coverage through an employer, and a year of premiums pays off mainly for those who use the glasses or contacts allowance.

VSP, a not-for-profit vision benefits manufacturer founded in 1955, is based in Rancho Cordova, California, and sells these plans directly on its own website. It counts more than 41,000 eye doctors in its network, and the Better Business Bureau rates Vision Service Blueprint, the company’s legal name, A+.

All four looks renew their benefits every 12 months and have no waiting period, so you can book an exam the day you enroll. They differ in what lens upgrades cost and whether an exam is covered.

Standard covers the basics with two copays, which are flat fees you pay at the office. You pay one at the exam and one for the glasses, and the plan costs the least of the three that include an exam.

A frame inside the allowance costs nothing beyond the copays. VSP puts the average frame at $253 without insurance, and by our math the allowance and the 20% discount leave about $82 of that to pay.

According to recent reports, both plans keep Standard’s exam, glasses copay, and allowance and cut what lens upgrades cost. That matters most for progressive lenses, which correct near and far vision with no visible line, and which VSP prices at $504 for a custom pair without insurance.

VSP’s plan page lists typical prices of $30 a month for EasyOptions and $35 for Enhanced, against $17 for Standard.

EyewearOnly drops the exam for a typical $12 a month. It keeps the $25 glasses copay and gives a $120 allowance for frames or contacts, or $140 on featured frame brands, but your prescription has to come from an exam in the past 12 months. It suits someone who already has a current prescription.

VSP prices each proposal by where you live and demonstrates your rate after you enter a ZIP code. These quotes came from its site on Nov. 16, 2026, for one adult unless noted:.

Recent findings suggest that in California, every plan but Standard also carried a $1.50 monthly membership in the Healthy Vision Association, a discount program some plans require. The Newly introduced York quotes had no such fee, and California’s Standard, EasyOptions, and Enhanced prices didn’t change between the 30-to-44 and 64-and-older age brackets.

You can pay for the year up front or in 12 monthly installments, but the monthly option is still a one-year contract. The plan renews automatically on the card you enrolled with, and VSP sends a reminder 60 days before. You can switch plans only in the first 30 days, and only if you haven’t used any benefits.

Industry observers note that take one adult on Standard in Rancho Cordova who gets an exam and one pair of single-vision glasses with a $150 frame. Without insurance, VSP’s own figures put that exam at $214 and the lenses at $118. The plan’s year costs $244, $204 in premiums plus the $15 and $25 copays, against $482 without it, a $238 saving.

Recent findings suggest that buying the plan for an exam alone costs $219 a year on Standard in Rancho Cordova and $165 in Newly introduced York, premiums plus the $15 copay. VSP puts an uninsured exam at $214, but All About Vision’s survey of 100 eye care practices found an average of about $110, and $93 at retail chains, so at those prices you’d pay less without the plan.

In Rancho Cordova, EasyOptions costs $167 a year more than Standard, fee included, and cuts the $175 progressive copay to $0, for a net gain of about $8. In Latest York, Enhanced costs $66 a year more than Standard and caps progressives at $55, which saves $120 on them for a net gain of $54.

The IRS counts eye exams and prescription glasses as medical expenses, so the copays and any frame cost above the allowance are a good use of flexible spending account money before it expires.

At an in-network office you tell the staff you have VSP, pay the copays, and file nothing. VSP lists Visionworks and Eyemart Express stores in its network, and members can use their benefits on Eyeconic, VSP’s online eyewear store. Costco’s optical departments are out of network for these looks, and VSP’s own pages disagree about Walmart, so check a store in VSP’s doctor search before you book.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Choose TurboTax if you want tax software that walks you through every question, or a tax expert to answer them, check your return, or file it for you.
  • Doing your own taxes saves a preparer’s fee, but it leaves you to judge whether every answer is right.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Choose TurboTax if you want tax software that walks you through every question, or a tax expert to answer them, check your return, or file it for you. If you’d fill in the forms on your own, file with a free program that covers them instead, since every TurboTax tier beyond simple returns charges a fee.

Doing your own taxes saves a preparer’s fee, but it leaves you to judge whether every answer is right. TurboTax is built around that worry. Its interview turns tax forms into plain questions about your year, and each step up in price adds more help, from a tax expert who answers questions as you go to one who prepares and files the whole return.

TurboTax is made by Intuit, the Mountain View, California, organization that started in 1983 with the Quicken money manager and also makes Credit Karma and QuickBooks. TurboTax brought in $5.3 billion in Intuit’s fiscal year that ended July 31, 2026, and 53% of that came from TurboTax Live, its tax-expert services.

TurboTax Online comes in three levels of help, priced by how complex your return is and how much of the work you hand off: do it yourself, Expert Assist, and Expert Full Service. TurboTax hadn’t posted prices for 2026 returns when this review was written in November 2026, so the prices below are what it charges for 2025 returns. Last season, those prices covered returns filed by March 31, and TurboTax expected to charge more from April 1. You pay the price in effect the day you print or e-file.

In a recent development, the do-it-yourself and Expert Assist tiers share one interview. In place of form lines, it asks about your year, such as whether you own a home, have children, or gave to charity, and fills in the forms from your answers. Intuit Assist, its AI helper, answers questions along the way, and a tool called CompleteCheck reviews the whole return for errors before you file.

In a recent development, you can snap a photo of a tax form, upload it, or import it straight from your employer or financial institution. If you used TurboTax Online last year, signing in with the same user ID carries your information over. Switchers can transfer last year’s Form 1040 as a PDF from other providers, including H&R Block, TaxAct, and TaxSlayer.

The do-it-yourself tiers differ by which parts of a return they handle, and the two paid ones charge $64 for each state return.

Sources indicate that enlisted active-duty members and reservists, E-1 through E-9, file federal and state returns free in any of these tiers with a W-2 from the Defense Finance and Accounting Service. Officers, veterans, retirees, and National Guard members don’t qualify, and the discount doesn’t apply to the expert tiers.

Returns for an S corporation, a partnership, or a multi-member limited liability company (LLC) go through TurboTax’s business service, TurboTax Experts for Business.

It has been revealed that expert Assist is the same software with a tax expert on call. You can reach one by phone, live chat, or one-way video, where you see the expert but they can’t see you, and share your screen so the expert can guide you. Before you file, an expert gives the whole return a final review. If the return needs significant advice or actual preparation, the expert may have to sign as its preparer and take primary responsibility for it.

Last season, experts were available seven days a week from Jan. 5 through April 20, 5 a.m. to 9 p.m. Pacific time, and customers could keep asking questions through Dec. 31 of the year they filed.

In a recent development, full Service hands the whole return to a dedicated tax expert. You upload your documents, and the expert prepares the return, walks you through it, then signs and files it. TurboTax says its expert files only a return they believe is 100% correct.

According to recent reports, it starts at $129 for one federal return with one W-2, plus $69 per state, and the final price depends on the forms your return needs. You get an estimate before the expert starts. You can work with the expert by phone, one-way video, or messages, or in person where a local expert is offered, at one of more than 500 TurboTax Expert offices.

TurboTax’s calculation and refund guarantees last for what Intuit calls the life of a return, seven years from the day you file it with TurboTax.

Audit support is information only, so no one from TurboTax represents you before the IRS. For that, it sells Audit Defense, an add-on from a separate company, Tax Audit, for an extra fee.

Paying TurboTax out of your federal refund can add a $40 service fee. An early-refund option deposits your federal refund up to five days before the IRS would, for a fee taken from the refund, though TurboTax’s early-refund page doesn’t say how much that fee is. You aren’t charged if the money doesn’t arrive at least a day early.

According to recent reports, turboTax has also offered a Refund Advance, an interest-free loan from WebBank against your expected refund, with no loan fees. Last season it lent up to half the refund, to a maximum of $4,000, or up to the whole refund and $10,000 for Full Service customers. Filers needed an expected federal refund of at least $500, and the money went into a Credit Karma Money checking account.

You pay only when you print or e-file, and once you do, you give up the right to a refund of the price.

TurboTax is the tax software to pay for when you want the most guidance, or a tax expert, on your return. Its interview and imports suit filers who find tax forms confusing. Its expert tiers put a professional on the return to answer questions, review it, or prepare it, and its guarantees cover the expert’s mistakes as well as the software’s.

Industry observers note that its weakness is price. Every tier past Free Edition’s simple returns charges a fee, so anyone who’d fill in the forms without help pays for guidance they won’t use. Intuit’s own Credit Karma Tax indicates it will charge $0 for a 2026 federal return. Pay TurboTax’s prices for its interview if tax forms confuse you, or for an expert who checks or prepares your return.

⏱️ ~14 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • As a man of Science, I’m supposed to hide my enthusiasm about this somewhat controversial subject, and instead direct you only to the peer-reviewed studies.
  • But man, I feel like I’ve stumbled upon the fountain of youth here.
  • According to recent reports, I’ve been interested in optimization and trying to get the most out of my body and mind since I was a little kid.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

As a man of Science, I’m supposed to hide my enthusiasm about this somewhat controversial subject, and instead direct you only to the peer-reviewed studies.

But man, I feel like I’ve stumbled upon the fountain of youth here. And the more I dig into the details and the hype and controversy surrounding the field of Hormone Replacement therapy, the more I need to share the word about it to my fellow middle-aged people (both men and women).

According to recent reports, I’ve been interested in optimization and trying to get the most out of my body and mind since I was a little kid. I started vacuuming up all the training and nutrition books and magazines I could find while I was just a teenager, and that field still remains a favorite of mine over 30 years later. And if you’re a long-time reader here you’ve been reminded plenty of times of this interest, because health has always been the very heart of Mustachianism.

According to recent reports, but a funny thing has been happening in the last ten years: even as I kept honing the healthy living habits and trying my best to improve, there seemed to be a force pulling me back almost as hard. So despite working a bit harder and smarter every year, I still felt myself riding a gradually declining tide of energy, motivation, and physical stamina.

“Perhaps this is just what it means to grow old”, I thought to myself,.

“But I’m still gonna keep fighting it!”.

It has been revealed that yet there was one thing that didn’t quite fit. Why was I having this decline in energy, when some of my older friends weren’t? And why was I still seeing people out there in their 50s, 60s and well beyond doing things that I felt too tired to do today?

According to recent reports, one of these tireless friends is a guy named Kevin, who is the personification of the highly energetic successful middle-aged man. He’s a semi-retired serial entrepreneur (and extreme rock climber) who lives in Boulder. And through an interesting twist of fate, in April of 2025 he invited me out for a hike right around the time I was doing all this wondering. And during this hike (and climb) he told me about his latest venture, a boutique men’s health manufacturer that specializes in helping men just like us get their youth back through the process of testosterone replacement therapy.

According to recent reports, long story short: his ideas planted a seed in my head, which led to a bunch of research and a growing interest in trying TRT myself. I had of course heard about the process, but for some reason never considered doing it until I heard Kevin’s enthusiasm: he had been on it for several years, and according to him it is a “night and day difference” in all the things you want in life: energy, focus, thinking speed, and of course physical health.

Another convenient twist of fate is that I happen to be dating an REI doctor – a Reproductive Endocrinologist and Infertility specialist who has two board certifications in exactly the relevant bodily systems that are affected by these hormones. And while she was initially skeptical that I needed more Testosterone (and in her practice she regularly sees the downsides of men taking the stuff too early in life and thus compromising their own fertility), she has followed along and helped me learn at each step of this process, eventually becoming fully in support of the program.

Industry observers note that so I signed up as a test customer for Kevin’s fresh company, which is called Bolt Health. I worked with their doctor to get a baseline blood test and review my numbers compared to all the past tests I’ve collected, and as it turned out, my levels had been dropping consistently over the years, and the latest test was by far the lowest ever.

Even more telling, my age-related drop in Testosterone was correlating perfectly with my decline in energy and motivation:.

Sources indicate that the next step was a prescription for a tiny daily dose of supplemental T, which arrived at my house the next week along with instructions for how to use it. And so began the journey.

Now let’s jump forward seven months to the present day as I write this.

And wow, what a great year it has been! I only wish I had known and tried this a few years earlier, because I’m getting a lot more out of my life.

It’s not a night-and-day difference for me, but more like a 50% boost in overall youthfulness and energy. The biggest subjective change is that I just don’t have sucky tired days anymore, which was the main problem with my life before: wasting too much of my precious freedom due to not having the energy to enjoy it.

Sources indicate that this is why I’ve become somewhat of an evangelist for hormone replacement therapy for people from about age 45 onwards. It won’t work for everyone – if your levels are already pretty high, you don’t get the same boost. Two of my male friends tried TRT and quit because they didn’t notice any benefit. But these same two guys already had plenty of energy to begin with, which is usually a sign that the body has what it needs.

It turns out I am very late to this party. Although Testosterone supplementation started out as a niche practice in the 1940s, from the 2010s onward it has been everywhere.

TRT is the reason you see every actor suddenly showing up buff overnight for their superhero roles and it’s also why so many of today’s CEOs don’t look anything like yesterday’s CEOs.

It has been revealed that in many cases, it has gone too far with young men using it just to gain muscle for the beach or the football field, and questionable online providers (aka “Prescription Mills”) handing out prescriptions to anyone with a valid credit card – with profit as their sole motive. It became overhyped in certain pockets of Bro Culture, where every Bro eventually receives the advice “Bro! You need to get on the T!” from another Bro, and therefore does it. And some of this reputation surely contributed to my own skepticism.

Industry observers note that but there’s a lot of valid science behind TRT, if you’re the right candidate and you take the right dosage. And because of that, I feel it is probably under-hyped in my own demographic, the Nerdy Tech Worker Semi Retired Dad contingent. And that’s why I’m writing this blog post, because there are a lot of us out there.

Many of us just tend to work with what we were given, and accept that aging means slowing down. And for those of us already enjoying an early retirement, we have the option of unlimited rest and recuperation time, so who really cares if we get tired a bit more often? After all, what better way to flex one’s wealth than with a decadent Tuesday Afternoon Nap while everyone else is stuck in the office?

Sources indicate that while this seemingly healthy attitude has a lot of positive aspects, it can also mask a real problem which may be easily fixable. Because sometimes, the only thing that’s even better than an afternoon nap, is having the energy and motivation to go out for an afternoon hike, bike ride or adventure with friends. More energy is also pretty darned useful if you’re still raising kids or trying to do well in your career as a person over 45.

How it Actually Works (and What Happened to Me).

Recent findings suggest that distilling all of the fluffy discussion above into the simplest possible answer: TRT means using a tiny needle to inject a few drops of clear liquid just below the surface of your skin. And you do this by yourself at home, ideally once every morning.

Here’s one of the baby needles I use for my daily dose.The typical serving is less than one tenth of a milliliter, which is only a few drops.

Recent findings suggest that and while the term “needle” sounds scary to some, this is very different from the monstrosities they use to draw blood from your veins. This one is so miniature that you don’t need special training to use it, and you usually don’t even feel it.

So I began doing this to myself on May 1st of this year, while keeping a daily journal of my results along the way. The results seemed to be almost immediate in all the promised areas, but I know how powerful the Placebo Effect can be so I kept my skeptic’s hat on to see what would happen in the long run.

Sources indicate that I was seeing increased energy and motivation as well as lean weight gain through the whole spring and summer, but I remember the first truly shocking observation happened during a mountain vacation in July. I was part of a multi-family trip with lively adults, chaotic kids, early mornings, late nights with a few drinks, very intense high altitude sunshine and nonstop physical activities. It was just the type of situation that would drain my energy pretty swiftly in the past.

But on day three I went out on a solo mountain bike ride to explore the area, and as I was climbing a long ascent with the blazing sun cooking me from every angle I just somehow kept having plenty of energy to keep climbing. Then I came down and joined the group for a few games of full-sun pickleball, biked back up the mountain to our cabin, and the story of unlimited energy went on from there.

“Hot Damn”, I thought to myself, “I don’t know whose youthful and tireless body I have inherited here but I’d sure like to keep it!”.

In August, the Bolt Health program scheduled a follow-up blood test for me and sure enough, my Testosterone levels had been boosted from 415 to 730ng/dL, bringing me from the low side of normal to the higher side.

Many labs define “normal” as anywhere between 300 and 1000, which seems strange to me given the huge effect this hormone has on your wellbeing. It’s a bit like saying “Most cars have between 90 and 300 horsepower, so it doesn’t really matter what engine you have”.

I mean yeah, either one will still get you down the road, but which one would you rather be driving?

According to recent reports, since then, it has just been more of the same good results. My improvements ramped up and then just stayed there – so I’m operating at a latest, much higher and more enjoyable level of functioning. Energy and motivation are no longer a problem, and I even find myself willing to make longer-term plans again (before this everything beyond same-day planning felt overwhelming). And my body seems to just want to gain strength and size with any excuse. Heavy weights feel lighter and the hard manual labor I still like to spend my time on feels easier for longer. It’s nice to be young again!

So Why Doesn’t Everyone Do This?

Industry observers note that when you dig into the details, hormone replacement is mired in a soup of both real and incorrect information about both its benefits and its risks. And then our well-meaning medical establishment locks this whole container of soup deep in the cabinet with a label that notes, “Needs Further Study”. But if you summarize the findings on both sides of the issue, you’ll see this:.

Stuff you should do BEFORE trying TRT:.

Industry observers note that the modern American Lifestyle is a Testosterone and Health Crusher. It’s a miracle that anybody feels good ever with the crap that people do to their bodies. So if you’re not already doing all the simple, natural, outdoor things that naturally boost your health, energy, and hormone levels, you’ll want to start with these first. You can find a pretty complete list on my oft-cited Badassity Tracker page.

In a recent development, since I was already doing all of these things pretty consistently, I felt ready to take the next step and at least consider hormone supplementation. But wait, there’s more!

Industry observers note that many of the problems above are more likely to appear when the body is flooded with too much testosterone. In the bad old days, TRT was administered by sticking a pellet beneath your skin or injecting a large amount into the butt which then gets used up over the next several weeks. One friend recounted a story of extreme moodiness when the pellet was first implanted, ramping down to tiredness by the time the hormone was all gone.

It has been revealed that more modern providers like Bolt have fixed this problem by breaking the dose into much smaller servings which you administer each day. The idea is that your levels remain stable, and you need a lot less overall which reduces side effects.

For my part, I have not had any of the negative side effects because I was a pretty ideal candidate in the first place: 50 years old with depressed Testosterone levels but an otherwise healthy lifestyle and no risk factors.

In a recent development, my hope in sharing this article is to be transparent and hopefully take some of the stigma out of this subject of other people who might benefit. Because in our modern over-connected world, everybody has an opinion on your life, even when you didn’t ask them.

Recent findings suggest that and it’s not just men – many women in this same age group benefit from Estrogen replacement (and there are even interesting stories about female testosterone supplementation in certain situations as this author shares). The point is that aging is normal, but in some cases there’s a pretty easy way to make it slower.

According to recent reports, the great news is that Testosterone itself is a cheap and widely available substance, typically under $50 per month even for people like me without conventional insurance or drug coverage. The expensive part (here in the US) is just the doctor stuff – consultations, blood tests, ongoing analysis and prescription renewals and so on.

The firm that I used is positioned as a premium provider, bundling these services along with a bunch of other men’s health perks and deliveries for a few hundred dollars, which is expensive relative to most other parts of my budget, but still cheap if I consider the life and financial benefits of being 20-50% more energetic and productive.

If you want to be on this program, your final decision will hinge on your income, insurance coverage if applicable, whether your existing doctor can already help you, and how much service and advice you’re willing to pay for.

Note: I decided not to become a Bolt health affiliate because I wanted to write this article without conflict of interest. And I can honestly say, Bolt’s product and service seem great to me because I know and trust the people who run it. But  it’s also the only one I’ve tried. So I don’t know much about the competition and there may be other good options out there. At the very minimum, you can always try one service and switch to another if you don’t like the first one.

In a recent development, I’ve got lots more to say on money and early retirement, and lots of interesting projects in the works now too. So I’m thankful to have stumbled upon this booster for all aspects of life, so I can do more of everything else, for even more decades than I had expected.

I wish this same type of good fortune for you, however you create it.

In the Comments: Do you have questions about hormone replacement or anything else in this article? I’ll try to invite Kevin, Dr. Sean Bender and other knowledgeable people to contribute and answer questions as well.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Use TurboTax Experts for Business if you’re a sole proprietor or run an S corp or partnership and want a tax expert to check your return or prepare it. For an S corp, doing the entry yourself in Expert Assist Business costs less than half what Full Service charges. A C corporation can’t use it, so hire a CPA.

It has been revealed that for a business owner, the business return is the hardest part of tax season to do alone. A sole proprietor adds Schedule C, the form that reports business profit, to a personal return. An S corporation’s Form 1120-S and a partnership’s Form 1065 are due a month before personal returns, each with a Schedule K-1 that reports every owner’s share of the profit. TurboTax Experts for Business lets you prepare that return with an expert on call, or hand it to an expert who prepares, signs, and files it.

Recent findings suggest that turboTax belongs to Intuit, which began operating in 1983 and is based in Mountain View, California. TurboTax brought Intuit $5.3 billion in revenue in the fiscal year that ended July 31, 2026. TurboTax states it has more than 10,000 business tax experts and matches each owner with one who knows the owner’s industry. The experts report an average of 13 years of tax experience. The prices below are the ones it still listed in mid-November 2026, for 2025 returns, since it hadn’t yet posted prices for 2026 returns.

TurboTax prices each tier by the return your business files. Expert Assist and Full Service both include unlimited expert help by phone, chat, or one-way video, from 5 a.m. to 9 p.m. Pacific time every day of tax season.

You prepare the return yourself in TurboTax Online and contact an expert whenever a question comes up, from entering income and expenses to finding the deductions your industry can take. Before you file, an expert can review the whole return with you. Last season’s prices were:.

Those prices held for sole proprietors who filed by March 31 and for S corps and partnerships that filed by April 30, with late-season prices after that. If your return needs so much help that the expert ends up preparing it, IRS rules can require the expert to sign as preparer, and TurboTax’s terms say you may then have to switch to Full Service.

A dedicated expert matched to your industry starts with a video call, prepares the return, and walks you through it before signing and filing. Last season, an S corp or partnership return cost $1,549, plus $69 for each state. A sole proprietor’s price started at $249, which TurboTax states covers a W-2, Form 1040, Schedule C, and quarterly tax estimates. More forms cost more, and you get an estimate before work begins. Sole proprietors can also meet their expert in person at one of TurboTax’s Expert offices.

According to recent reports, for a sole proprietor with just a W-2 and a Schedule C, Full Service started only $20 above Expert Assist, $249 against $229, though its price rises as forms are added. For an S corp or partnership, handing off the return cost $910 more, $1,549 against $639. Since Expert Assist already includes an expert to ask and a final review, that $910 buys the expert’s time doing the preparation.

Industry observers note that full Service won’t do your bookkeeping, though. TurboTax’s terms require fully reconciled books, meaning records that match your bank and card statements, and let the expert refuse to start until they do. They also limit Full Service to businesses with a December 31 year-end, and new customers can’t use it for a business’s final return. If you can’t finish by the deadline, your expert files Form 7004, the IRS’s extension request for business returns, which adds six months.

This tier is a subscription for sole proprietors and single-member LLCs (limited liability companies) who want one expert all year. Your expert reconciles your books in QuickBooks each quarter and works out your quarterly estimated tax payments. You also get quarterly planning sessions, a check on whether another business structure would cut your taxes, and your return filed through Full Service at no extra cost. TurboTax’s terms leave tax planning out of its other tiers.

It costs $99 a month, including a QuickBooks Simple Start subscription billed alongside it, or $1,069 billed yearly, which TurboTax notes saves $119. You can try it free for 30 days. It’s open only to owners new to QuickBooks, and an S corp and partnership version at $199 a month is listed as coming soon. The estimates leave out sales and payroll taxes, and canceling brings no refund for the rest of the billing period.

Sources indicate that experts for Business prepares Schedule C for sole proprietors and single-member LLCs, Form 1120-S for S corps, and Form 1065 for partnerships and multi-member LLCs. It won’t prepare Form 1120, the return a C corporation files to pay its own income tax, or one for a business taxed as a C corporation. Trusts and estates, nonprofits, and returns needing more than five state filings are out too.

In a recent development, A C corporation that wants a professional needs a CPA or another paid preparer. One doing its own return can use TurboTax Business, TurboTax’s Windows desktop software, which prepares C corporation, trust, and estate returns as well as S corp and partnership returns. It has no expert to ask, and TurboTax’s audit support guarantee doesn’t cover it.

Sources indicate that S corp and partnership returns come due early. The IRS’s tax calendar puts their deadline on the 15th day of the third month after the tax year ends. For a business whose tax year ends December 31, the 2026 return is due Monday, March 15, 2027, and Form 7004 extends that six months. TurboTax’s pages still showed March 16, the 2026 deadline, which fell a day late because March 15, 2026, was a Sunday. A sole proprietor’s Schedule C is due with the personal return on April 15.

It has been revealed that the owner’s personal return belongs to TurboTax’s personal software. A sole proprietor can also get expert help on Schedule C there, in Expert Assist Premium, which listed at $209 last season against $229 for Expert Assist Business. S corp and partnership owners who file the business return first get 20% off one 2026 personal federal return in TurboTax Online, state fees excluded.

Recent findings suggest that turboTax backs business returns with what it calls the Business Tax Guarantee, and S corp and partnership returns add representation in an audit. Each piece covers something different:.

Audit Defense has limits of its own. TaxAudit’s membership terms rule out businesses with more than $5 million in gross receipts, meaning total sales before costs. They also cover income tax audits only, not payroll or sales tax audits, and they don’t include representation in court.

TurboTax Experts for Business is a good fit for a sole proprietor or a small S corp or partnership that wants an expert to check or prepare its return. A sole proprietor with a simple Schedule C should check the Full Service price first, since it started just $20 above Expert Assist’s last season. An S corp or partnership gets the better value from Expert Assist Business, with an industry-matched expert, a final review, and Audit Defense for $639, against $1,549 for Full Service.

Industry observers note that it’s the wrong fit for a C corporation, which needs a CPA or desktop software, and for owners whose books aren’t reconciled. S corp and partnership owners who keep their own books should open an Expert Assist Business return well before the March 15, 2027 deadline.
