📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, book TurboTax Experts if you want a tax expert to prepare and sign your return face to face and one of its 500-plus offices is near you. It costs what TurboTax’s experts charge online, but the starting price covers one W-2 and a Form 1040, so get every form priced before the expert starts.

According to recent reports, turboTax built its name on software you fill in yourself. Its offices work the other way around. You sit down with a TurboTax expert and hand over your documents, and the expert prepares the return, reviews it with you, signs it as the preparer, and files it.

Intuit, founded in 1983 and based in Mountain View, California, added 200 TurboTax offices for the 2026 filing season, and its office finder now lists more than 500. TurboTax customers gave Expert Full Service 4.8 out of 5 in more than 108,000 reviews from 2026, posted on TurboTax’s own site. The Better Business Bureau gives Intuit an F, citing 35 complaints the firm didn’t answer and 32 it didn’t resolve, out of more than 4,600 filed against Intuit in the past three years.

TurboTax sells this as Expert Full Service, the product it also offers online, with the meeting moved to an office.

TurboTax Expert offices take appointments only and stay open year-round. The office finder lists more than 500, from 72 in California to one each in states such as Alaska, Maine, and Oregon, and none in Vermont or Wyoming. TurboTax counts an in-person expert as local when the office is within 50 miles of your ZIP code, and if you’d rather meet online, it matches you with an expert in your state.

It has been revealed that turboTax stores take walk-ins as well as appointments. You can drop in with a question, start your return yourself with an expert’s guidance, or hand it off. Intuit’s February 2026 announcement listed stores in six metro areas: Latest York, Los Angeles, Chicago, Seattle, Dallas, and Phoenix. Hours vary by location, and TurboTax indicates its local service runs nights and weekends during tax season.

Every return starts at a federal base price that covers one W-2 and one Form 1040, and in person you pay from the same price list as online. TurboTax’s Full Service price list sets that base at $129 late in the season and after April 1, and at $89 early in the season, without saying when early season ends. Each state return adds $69, or $49 early. Most other forms carry a fee of their own.

By our math, a homeowner with a mortgage and one W-2 who itemizes deductions and files one state return pays $318 late in the season. That’s the $129 base plus $40 for the mortgage interest form, $80 for Schedule A, and $69 for the state. Early in the season, the same return costs $258.

Sources indicate that your expert gives you an estimate before starting, based on what you report and the documents you upload, and confirms any change with a final price before filing. You pay nothing until the expert files, and you can leave at any point before you pay. Paying the fee out of your refund can add $40 more.

Sources indicate that turboTax doesn’t publish the credentials of the expert you’ll get. Its blog notes its expert community includes CPAs, enrolled agents (tax specialists the IRS licenses), and other experienced tax experts, so the person preparing your return may hold no credential at all. The years of experience on its pages are self-reported.

The credential matters if the IRS questions your return. Under IRS rules, CPAs, enrolled agents, and attorneys can represent you on any matter, while other preparers can do so only in limited cases or not at all. You can look up a preparer’s credential in the IRS’s Directory of Federal Tax Return Preparers.

Sources indicate that turboTax matches you with an expert by your location and tax situation. You can’t pick one by name, but you can ask for a fresh match at any time, and you can request the same expert next year if they still work for Intuit and are available.

TurboTax’s Expert Full Service Guarantee covers the expert’s work. If your expert’s error as the signed preparer leads to a penalty or interest charge from the IRS or your state, TurboTax pays it, though you still owe any extra tax. If another preparer later files an amended return that gets you a bigger refund or a smaller tax bill, TurboTax refunds what you paid for Full Service.

TurboTax also guarantees its calculations, your maximum refund, and audit support for the seven-year life of the return. Audit support means one-on-one answers from a tax professional, and TurboTax won’t represent you before the IRS. For representation, you’d buy Audit Defense, a separate add-on from TaxResources, Inc.

Industry observers note that the first meeting is a free consultation, in person or online, where an expert reviews your situation and answers your questions with no commitment to file. Filing with TurboTax then takes five steps.

Sources indicate that bring a government-issued ID for each person on the return if you blueprint to file at the appointment. Same-day filing needs every document uploaded first and depends on the expert’s schedule.

After you file, the office stays your tax contact all year, for consultations, prior-year returns, amended returns, and IRS notices. An amended return on Form 1040-X carries no form fee.

TurboTax sells the same service online, where your expert works with you by phone, message, or one-way video, in which you see the expert but the expert can’t see you. The price list and guarantees don’t change, so the office is worth the trip only when a face-to-face meeting matters to you.

TurboTax’s own software lets you file a simple return free or fill in a harder one yourself, and its Expert Assist tiers add an expert who answers questions and reviews the return before you file.

H&R Block starts in-office preparation at $99 plus a state fee, against TurboTax’s $129 late-season base plus its own. Its offices also take walk-ins, which TurboTax leaves to its stores. Choosing between TurboTax and H&R Block also comes down to their software and online help, not only their offices.

Sources indicate that IRS-certified volunteers at Volunteer Income Tax Assistance sites prepare returns for free, generally for people who make about $70,244 or less, though each site may set its own limit. Every return they prepare gets a quality review before it’s filed.

Sole proprietors can use TurboTax Experts, since Schedule C is part of the personal return, but an S corporation’s or a partnership’s own return goes to a separate product, TurboTax Experts for Business.

In a recent development, turboTax Experts puts a tax preparer across the desk for what TurboTax charges for the same work online. You see a quote before the expert starts, pay only once the return is filed, and have TurboTax cover the penalties its expert’s errors cause, from an office that stays open after April.

In a recent development, it’s a poor fit for a simple return that free software or a volunteer site would handle, and for anyone who wants a CPA or an enrolled agent by name. Book the free consultation if an office is near you, and ask for the price with every form you’ll file before the expert starts.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that choose QuickBooks Online if your accountant already works in it or your business tracks inventory or projects. Prepares with accountant access cost $38 to $340 a month after three discounted months, so if you mostly send invoices, a cheaper plan or app does that for less.

It has been revealed that picking accounting software is mostly a decision about who else will work in your books. If a bookkeeper or accountant closes your books each month or files your business return, using the program they already know saves time on both sides. If nobody else logs in, you pay for collaboration you never use.

Industry observers note that quickBooks Online is the cloud accounting software Intuit sells to small businesses. Intuit, founded in 1983 and based in Mountain View, California, also makes TurboTax and notes about 100 million customers use its products. It says 650,000 accountants worldwide use its platform, and every proposal from Simple Start up includes free logins for two or three of yours. QuickBooks customers are also paying more. Intuit’s fiscal 2026 results, for the year that ended July 31, 2026, show QuickBooks Online Accounting revenue up 23%. Intuit said the fourth quarter’s 20% gain came from customers paying more on average, more customers, and changes in which plans they buy.

QuickBooks Online comes in six plans. QuickBooks Free and QuickBooks Lite are for one person working alone, while the four business plans, Simple Start through Advanced, add accountant access and, from Essentials up, more users. Each business strategy includes everything in the one below it, so your choice comes down to how many people need logins and whether you track inventory or projects.

Fresh customers on a monthly proposal choose between 50% off for 3 months and a 30-day free trial, then pay the plan’s current price each month until they cancel, with no annual contract. By our math, the discount saves $70 in year one. Over the first 12 months, Plus costs $1,470 with it (three months at $70, then nine at $140) and $1,540 with the trial (11 paid months at $140).

Not every business needs Simple Start. If you mostly send invoices, QuickBooks Lite handles them for $20 a month without accountant access, and Wave’s free Starter blueprint covers unlimited invoices, estimates, bills, and bookkeeping records. If your team needs more logins but no inventory tracking, compare Xero, which charges no per-user license fees.

It has been revealed that every strategy pulls in transactions from the bank and card accounts you connect, one bank on Free and two on Lite. From Simple Start up, QuickBooks copies the categories you choose and applies them to newly introduced transactions automatically. Intuit Intelligence, Intuit’s name for its AI tools, does more at each level:.

Intuit still calls Intuit Intelligence a beta release, so its features and limits can change. You choose which tasks run on their own and can undo what the AI did. Only admin users get the chat, and each initiative caps how much they can use it each month.

Industry observers note that quickBooks Free caps invoices at two a month unless you qualify for and turn on QuickBooks Payments, which lets customers pay an invoice by card or bank transfer. Payments has no monthly fee, but each transaction costs:.

Recent findings suggest that bill pay comes with every business proposal. Intuit’s plan pages list five free standard ACH bill payments a month, an allotment they say may vary, and $0.50 for each one after that. Its Bill Pay page calls standard ACH free on every plan, so confirm the fee with Intuit before you pay more than five vendors a month that way. Checks cost $1.50, and Faster ACH, which usually arrives the next business day, costs $10. For $15 a month, Bill Pay Premium adds AI bill entry and unlimited e-filing of the 1099 forms you send contractors. Bill Pay Elite, at $45 a month, adds approval workflows and user roles, and it has come free with Advanced since Aug. 1, 2026.

Inventory and job costing start at Plus. Plus updates quantities on hand automatically, alerts you when an item needs reordering, drafts purchase orders, and turns them into bills when the goods arrive. Its project tools track labor, payroll, and expenses for each job, and it adds budgets and up to 40 classes and locations for sorting income and expenses. Advanced lifts that limit and adds custom reports and dashboards, two-way syncing with Excel, and an estimates-versus-actuals report for projects.

In a recent development, no QuickBooks Online proposal includes payroll. Intuit sells it separately as QuickBooks Workforce, at a monthly base fee plus a fee for each employee:.

Latest customers pay half the base fee for three months, but per-employee fees stay at full price. At full price, a five-person team on Workforce Payroll pays $85 a month, $50 plus $35 in employee fees.

Expert Assisted, at $59 a month after a 30-day free trial, gives you a bookkeeping expert to answer questions but not to work in your books. Full-Service Bookkeeping, with a dedicated bookkeeper doing the monthly work, starts at $300 a month after a one-time cleanup fee, and a cleanup alone starts at $600. Neither service prepares or files your taxes.

Phone support comes with every business initiative and is free during the trial, while QuickBooks Free gets chat. Advanced adds Priority Circle, a premium support line with on-demand training. The Better Business Bureau (BBB) gives Intuit an F, citing complaints it failed to answer or resolve. It logged more than 4,600 complaints against Intuit in the last three years, nearly 2,000 of them in the past 12 months. Those counts cover all of Intuit’s products, TurboTax and Mailchimp included, not QuickBooks alone.

Sources indicate that leaving QuickBooks takes planning. The Export data tool saves your reports and lists to a single .zip of Excel files. Estimates, purchase orders, attachments, and your chart of accounts (the list of categories your books use) export separately, and Intuit’s help page names two ways out, Excel or QuickBooks Desktop. After you cancel a paid initiative, you keep read-only access for a year to finish exporting. Cancel during or after a free trial, and Intuit keeps your data for 90 days.

QuickBooks Online is the safe pick when someone besides you works in the books. Your accountant gets in free, Plus handles inventory and job costing, and the account grows to 25 users on Advanced without a move. On the higher intends, its AI now does real cleanup and reconciliation work.

It’s poor value for a one-person business that mostly sends invoices. Simple Start’s $38 a month buys accountant access and reports that business won’t use, while QuickBooks Lite handles invoicing for $20 and Wave for nothing. The discounted price also doubles after the third month, and payroll costs extra. If your accountant already works in QuickBooks, pick the proposal that covers your headcount and budget for its full price from the fourth month.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, since 1972, Alaska to Patagonia has been a classic cycling route of 30,000km or more. At any given time, several ambitious cyclists are attempting it. But no one is doing it quite like Tobias Renggli of Lucerne, Switzerland.

The 23-year-old endurance athlete is not only pedaling the distance but also climbing the highest peak in each of the 35 countries he passes through. And although it’s part of the marketing rather than the adventure, the imagery so far — shot both by Renggli and by a film production group he belongs to called the Black Forest Collective — is stunning for such a difficult journey.

It has been revealed that northern lights. Photo: Tobias Renggli.

Industry observers note that despite his age, this is not Renggli’s first adventure. In 2022, at the age of 18, he cycled all 44 European countries within seven months, climbing the highest peak of each and camping every night. In 2024, he climbed the highest mountains of all 26 Swiss cantons in about three weeks.

Sources indicate that subzero cycling. Photo: Tobias Renggli.

Sources indicate that renggli began in April from Deadhorse, Alaska, on the shores of the Beaufort Sea — still deep winter at that latitude, though the long Arctic days had returned. Pedaling 1,200km in temperatures as low as -30˚C, he made his way to Talkeetna, then skied in for eight days while pulling a sled.

Industry observers note that he then summited 6,190m McKinley with his occasional partner, Heli Hofmann — the first party atop the peak this year, which meant they had to break trail through the deep snow. It took them 36 days.

According to recent reports, next, it was onto 5,959m Mount Logan, Canada’s highest peak. Again with Heli Hofmann but no guide, they summited in late June. This time, they were the last party of the year to summit Logan.

According to recent reports, renggli then cycled with another friend to Vancouver, took a two-week break after covering 3,000km and summiting two of the hardest peaks he would encounter, then continued alone through the U.S. Typically, he cycles 100 to 160km per day, with some shorter days.

Recent findings suggest that in Seattle. Photo: Tobias Renggli.

Industry observers note that unlike most Trans-America cyclists, he chose to take Baja California rather than mainland Mexico. Crossing Baja was more difficult than expected. He described temperatures exceeding 40°C and a 120km stretch toward Loreto that he began with only two liters of water.

In Death Valley. Photo: Tobias Renggli.

Later, near Ciudad Insurgentes, thunderstorms flooded the roads. At night, he carried his bicycle through a fast-moving, thigh-deep flood while vehicles turned back.

According to recent reports, renggli had intended to take no motorized transportation, only sailboats when confronted with water — he also wants to climb 12 high points in the Caribbean. However, this is such a massive undertaking that he’s not being too strict on himself. Although he skied into Denali, for example, he flew back out to Talkeetna. And from La Paz in Baja, he caught the ferry to Mazatlan on the mainland and continued from there.

Details have been sparse since Baja, but Renggli recently crossed into Guatemala. Presumably, he climbed 5,636m Pico de Orizaba before leaving Mexico and is now headed to 4,220m Volcán Tajumulco, Guatemala’s highest peak. He has been on the road for 202 days.

Reggli’s route and current location.

Zoe Financial Review – Free Matches With Vetted Fiduciaries, if You Have $150,000

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Use Zoe Financial if you have $150,000 or more to invest and want screened fiduciary advisors to interview at no cost.
  • Industry observers note that picking a financial advisor means trusting a stranger with your savings, and the title alone tells you nothing about their training, their fees, or who else pays them.
  • Zoe is a Upcoming York investment adviser, formed in 2016 and registered with the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) since 2019.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Use Zoe Financial if you have $150,000 or more to invest and want screened fiduciary advisors to interview at no cost. The advisor you hire pays Zoe, and the SEC fined it in 2026 for not fully disclosing why some advisors got its referrals, so check each match’s fees and record yourself.

Industry observers note that picking a financial advisor means trusting a stranger with your savings, and the title alone tells you nothing about their training, their fees, or who else pays them. Zoe Financial screens advisors for you and sets up calls with as many as three of them at no charge, because the advisor you hire pays Zoe instead.

Zoe is a Upcoming York investment adviser, formed in 2016 and registered with the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) since 2019. Its founder and CEO, Andres Garcia-Amaya, holds the Chartered Financial Analyst (CFA) charter and was a global market strategist at J.P. Morgan Asset Management. Zoe began matching people with advisors in 2018 and now runs that service at FindAnAdvisor.com as the Zoe Network. In 2023 and 2024 the network held between about 128 and 225 advisory firms, by the SEC’s count. Its Trustpilot profile indicates a 4.7 rating from 92 reviews, six of them from the past year. In September 2026, Zoe settled SEC charges over how it disclosed the conflicts behind its referrals.

According to recent reports, zoe’s service has three parts: the match, the screening behind it, and the investing platform Zoe’s advisors use for clients’ accounts. Matching and screening cost you nothing, but Zoe charges fees on the platform that can land on your bill.

Sources indicate that A two-minute form asks about your household income, your goals, what you own, and your ZIP code. Zoe’s algorithm then suggests up to three advisors, and you book free calls to interview them, though Zoe’s SEC brochure notes that some people get a single name.

Recent findings suggest that A concierge team books the calls and looks for a better fit if the first names miss. You’re never obligated to hire anyone, and most advisors in the network work remotely, so where you live doesn’t narrow the list.

The form doesn’t weigh your tolerance for risk or your full finances, the brochure claims, so the calls are where you judge fit.

According to recent reports, zoe sets no minimum to use the form, but its advisors take clients with at least $150,000 in investable assets and $100,000 in income, and some set a higher bar. Its average client has more than $750,000. With less to invest, a robo-advisor, an automated service that manages a fund portfolio for a small yearly fee, usually fits better. So do the kinds of advisors paid a flat fee or by the hour, whose fees don’t grow with your portfolio.

Sources indicate that zoe says every advisor in its network holds a Certified Financial Planner (CFP) certification, the CFA charter, or a certified public accountant (CPA) license, with five or more years of experience and a clean SEC record. Each is a fiduciary, legally bound to put your interests first, and Zoe says its matches don’t sell commission-paying products, such as some annuities and insurance policies.

Its SEC brochure describes a looser test. Zoe checks that a firm centers on financial planning, that some of its advisors hold a credential such as the CFA, CFP, or CPA, or a graduate business degree, and that it has no material disciplinary history. It reviews each advisor’s regulatory filings and rereads every firm’s brochure once a year.

What Zoe doesn’t check is how an advisor performs once you’ve hired one. Before your first call, look up each match’s record yourself. Ask, too, whether the advisor is fee-only, paid by you alone, since not every fiduciary is.

It has been revealed that zoe’s third step, after the form and the calls, is opening your accounts on its investing platform, debuted in 2023. Advisors in its referral program join by invitation and must keep a minimum level of client assets there, so expect the advisor you hire to suggest it.

Industry observers note that those are brokerage accounts held by Apex Clearing, which keeps the assets and settles the trades, and opened through Zoe’s sister brokerage, Zoe Securities. Trades in stocks, exchange-traded funds (ETFs), and mutual funds carry no commission. Your advisor can choose ready-made model portfolios from firms such as BlackRock, Vanguard, and State Street. The platform rebalances them automatically and can harvest tax losses, selling investments at a loss to offset taxable gains.

The accounts are yours, so leaving an advisor means moving them to another firm or hiring another advisor who uses Zoe’s platform.

Zoe doesn’t publish what its advisors charge, so the fee schedule each match hands you is the number to compare.

Zoe’s site notes you won’t pay to use its platform, while its client relationship summary, filed with the SEC, says you or your advisor will. Ask each match to put every fee, Zoe’s included, on the agreement you sign.

Say a match charges 1% a year, the rate Zoe’s own fee guide uses in its examples. On $150,000, that’s $1,500 a year, and on $750,000, it’s $7,500, before fund expenses or platform fees.

Recent findings suggest that zoe’s satisfaction guarantee is narrower than its FAQ makes it sound. The FAQ promises a refund of all advisor fees if you’re unhappy, but the terms cap it at one billing period of fees, a month’s or a quarter’s worth. You qualify only after three months of full advisory service, must ask within a 24-month window between hiring and leaving the advisor, and get nothing back for one-time or hourly planning.

When you hire a match, that advisor pays Zoe 15% to 35% of the fee it charges you, Zoe’s solicitation disclosure claims. Zoe collects that share for as long as you stay when the fee is a percentage of your assets, and for five years of a flat-fee planning arrangement. Some advisors pay a one-time referral fee instead. On a $7,500 yearly fee, Zoe’s share would come to $1,125 to $2,625 a year.

Zoe’s contracts bar advisors from charging referred clients more, so you’d pay the same fee walking in on your own. To screen advisors yourself, the National Association of Personal Financial Advisors (NAPFA) keeps an online directory of fee-only advisors you can sort by how they charge.

Recent findings suggest that that pay gives Zoe reasons to favor some advisors. Its share differs by firm, and some advisors pay just to join the network. Several advisory firms, Creative Planning and Mariner Wealth Advisors among them, own small stakes in Zoe, and some of its owners are in the network. Zoe’s own advisory arm competes for the same referrals, and Zoe earns platform fees from advisors who use its platform. Zoe claims its algorithm weighs none of this.

The SEC found that referrals didn’t always work that way. In a settled order of September 28, 2026, the agency said that in 2023 and 2024 Zoe didn’t tell users it had a financial stake in steering them to advisors using its upcoming platform. As that period went on, Zoe told advisors who wouldn’t adopt the platform that they’d be dropped from the network. It also found that Zoe’s statement that referrals rested solely on users’ answers was misleading, since salespeople often suggested other advisors. Clients who hired a network advisor in that period picked one the algorithm hadn’t first suggested about 46% of the time.

Zoe agreed, without admitting or denying the findings, to be censured, to stop such violations, and to pay a $450,000 penalty. It says it has since told salespeople not to recommend advisors of their own and hired a full-time chief compliance officer. Ask whoever books your calls how each advisor made your list.

In a recent development, zoe Financial is a sound starting point for anyone with $150,000 or more who wants a fiduciary advisor and doesn’t know where to begin. It narrows the field to screened, credentialed firms, books the interviews, and costs you nothing, and its contracts keep its cut of your advisor’s fee off your bill.

It’s a poor fit below that bar, and for anyone who wants a referral with no money riding on the outcome, since Zoe earns more from some advisors than others and the SEC found it didn’t fully disclose that. Treat each match as a candidate, not a recommendation. Ask why the advisor made your list, get the full fee schedule in writing with any platform fees on it, and check the record before you sign.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Australian grain farm manager Scott Gladman, 63, is attempting to swim the length of the Darling River, Australia’s third-longest river. It begins in Newly introduced South Wales and finishes at its confluence with the Murray River at Wentworth. Gladman believes he will be the first person to swim the entire 1,650km route.

In a recent development, gladman started on September 1 from near Brewarrina in far north Upcoming South Wales. At the outset, he budgeted 103 days to complete the swim, averaging around 16km per day. So far, he is largely on track. After 49 days, he has covered 660km, leaving just under 1,000km to go.

Recent findings suggest that interestingly, the expedition is not born from a love of endurance swimming. Gladman was inspired to find a fundraising challenge to support friends impacted by Motor Neuron Disease and Progressive Supranuclear Palsy, a rare form of Parkinson’s. Initially, he considered the Murray. “I just thought I could swim the Murray River, but people have done that,” he told ABC News. “No one has had a crack at the Darling.”.

Industry observers note that the location of the Darling River in Australia. Photo: Wikimedia Commons.

Gladman gave himself 18 months to train. In the summer, he swam in the Murray River at Boundary Bend, Victoria, and during winter he completed laps in indoor pools. Now out on the Darling, a support boat of family and friends keeps him company, alongside a canoeist.

“There’s no real form of communication, and I wear earplugs…he’ll [the canoeist] either have to hit me on the back of the head with a paddle to get my attention, or he’ll just start steering toward me, and that will push me one way or the other,” Gladman said.

According to recent reports, despite its length, the Darling River is sometimes so shallow that Gladman needs to float through sections on his back, or walk. The support boat also sometimes requires saving, with Gladman having to help clear a path through river debris:.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Open a Kraken account if you want crypto, U.S.
  • Industry observers note that buying crypto in a simple app is easy but costly.
  • In a recent development, kraken is the trading name of Payward Inc., founded in 2011, and it says more than 13 million people worldwide trust it.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Open a Kraken account if you want crypto, U.S. stocks, and pro-grade trading under one login, from an exchange that publishes proof of reserves. Place your regular buys on Kraken Pro rather than the app, whose 1% fee and built-in spread make it the account’s costliest way to trade.

Industry observers note that buying crypto in a simple app is easy but costly. Trading on an exchange’s order book, the live list of buy and sell offers, costs less but takes more know-how, and stocks usually sit at a separate brokerage. Kraken puts all three behind one login, so the decision that matters is where you place each trade.

In a recent development, kraken is the trading name of Payward Inc., founded in 2011, and it says more than 13 million people worldwide trust it. In the U.S., it’s licensed to transfer customers’ money in 46 jurisdictions and offers stock trading through Kraken Securities, a broker-dealer registered with the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC). It also publishes proof-of-reserves reviews, which check that it holds the crypto its clients’ balances show, a practice it says it began in 2014.

The account has five parts: a simple app, a pro exchange, stock trading, ways to earn on idle coins, and two companion apps.

According to recent reports, the Kraken app is the simple side of the account. You buy, sell, or convert crypto at the price it quotes, set recurring buys daily, weekly, or monthly on more than 200 coins, and pay by bank transfer, debit card, or PayPal. Kraken states it lists more than 600 cryptocurrencies, though it restricts 83 of them for U.S. clients. The app suits investors who buy now and then and don’t want to learn an order book.

According to recent reports, kraken Pro, on the same login, is the full exchange, with stop-loss and take-profit orders, charts with 25-plus trading and data widgets, a desktop app, and API access for your own trading software. Eligible U.S. traders can also trade on margin, borrowing against their crypto for positions worth up to 20 times their collateral on some coins, and trade perpetual futures, contracts with no expiration date. Both run through Kraken Derivatives US, a futures broker registered with the Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC), and Kraken warns that margin losses can exceed what you put up.

Industry observers note that the Kraken app and Kraken Pro also trade more than 11,000 U.S.-listed stocks and exchange-traded funds (ETFs) with no commission, through Kraken Securities, in every state Kraken serves. Orders placed outside market hours wait for the next session, Kraken Pro adds trading 24 hours a day on weekdays, and Kraken charges nothing on its end to move shares in from another broker.

Once you switch it on, Auto Earn stakes eligible idle coins, committing them to help run their blockchains in return for rewards. It pays weekly and keeps the coins free to trade or withdraw, and on coins that make you wait to unstake, it pays rewards on up to half of what you stake. Bonded staking pays more for locking coins up for a set term.

It has been revealed that rates on the biggest coins are low. Kraken estimates Auto Earn’s annual percentage yield (APY) at 0.02% for bitcoin and 1.47% for ether, before its commission. DeFi Earn puts USDC, a stablecoin pegged to the dollar, into vaults that lend it on blockchain lending markets for up to 5.33% APY, though the rate floats, the product isn’t regulated, and you can lose money.

Industry observers note that kraken Wallet is a free self-custody app, meaning you hold the keys to your coins instead of Kraken, on Bitcoin, Ethereum, Solana, and other networks. Krak, a separate money app, sends money free between Kraken owners and lets you spend through the Krak Card, a Visa debit card from Lead Bank. The card pays up to 2% cash back, at a rate set by the average assets you hold across Krak, Kraken, and Kraken Pro, and because Krak isn’t a bank, its balances carry no FDIC deposit insurance.

It has been revealed that the app’s convenience is the account’s biggest cost. Every app price includes a spread, a markup over the market rate that Kraken doesn’t publish and may keep, on top of these fees.

It has been revealed that counting fees alone, since Kraken doesn’t publish the app’s spread, here is what $500 of bitcoin a month costs by our math. The app charges $5 a month, or $60 a year. Kraken+ costs $59.88 a year on monthly billing, so it pays off once app trades top about $500 a month, or about $417 on the annual blueprint. Kraken Pro charges $2 for the same buy as a maker order or $4 as a taker order, and Kraken states Pro prices carry no hidden spread.

Sources indicate that if you want only bitcoin or ether as a long-term slice of a portfolio, a spot exchange-traded product (ETP) is the main alternative. It holds the coin itself and trades on a stock exchange, so you skip the crypto wallet and keys, though you pay the fund’s sponsor an ongoing fee that direct holders don’t.

Kraken says no custodial wallet it manages has been breached since its founding in 2011, and it keeps most client crypto offline, in cold storage in guarded facilities. Accounts sign in with passkeys and two-factor authentication and can’t be recovered by text message.

An independent accountant’s proof-of-reserves review for Sept. 30, 2026, found Kraken held 103.2% of its clients’ bitcoin and 100.7% of their ether. Kraken notes that such a review can’t rule out hidden claims on the coins or prove they weren’t borrowed, and it covers only the coins it names, not dollar balances.

In a recent development, crypto at Kraken carries neither FDIC deposit insurance nor the brokerage protection of the Securities Investor Protection Corporation (SIPC). Stocks are different. Kraken Securities is a member, and SIPC covers up to $500,000, including $250,000 in cash, if a member brokerage fails, though never market losses.

Sources indicate that kraken’s record with regulators is mixed. In 2023 it paid $30 million to settle SEC charges over its old U.S. staking program and shut that program down, relaunching U.S. staking as a new product in 2025. A separate SEC lawsuit claiming Kraken ran an unregistered securities exchange was dismissed for good in 2025.

Industry observers note that kraken serves every state except Newly introduced York and Maine, and some features run on shorter lists. Staking is open only in 37 states, Washington, D.C., and Puerto Rico, which by our count leaves out 11 states Kraken otherwise serves, including California, Texas, Illinois, and New Jersey. The Krak Card isn’t offered in Massachusetts or Indiana, and Krak’s cash transfers aren’t available in Indiana, Louisiana, Massachusetts, or Utah. Margin and perpetual futures go only to traders who meet Kraken’s eligibility rules.

Sources indicate that support runs around the clock by live chat and email, with phone calls only in select cases. Kraken calls you only after you’ve contacted it and arranged the call, so treat any other call, or a Kraken number found in a search ad, as a scam. Of Kraken’s 9,583 reviews on Trustpilot, 49% give one star and 33% give five, for a TrustScore of 3.1 out of 5.

Kraken is a strong pick for investors who want crypto, U.S. stocks, and serious trading tools in one account. Its best case is Kraken Pro’s low fees beside the beginner app, backed by proof of reserves and a clean custody record.

It’s the wrong account for Latest York and Maine residents, who can’t open one, and for anyone in the 11 other states without staking who wants rewards on idle coins. Long-term holders who want only bitcoin or ether can own them through a spot ETP instead. Everyone else should open the account and route regular buys through Kraken Pro, or add Kraken+ once app trades top about $500 a month.

#21689. Seven Alpine-Style Climbs Happening Now in Nepal

Seven Alpine-Style Climbs Happening Now in Nepal

📅 20 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (636 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Explorersweb

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that several small teams are attempting difficult climbs on Nepal’s 6,000 and 7,000m peaks.
  • This is what we know about the ongoing expeditions:.
  • Recent findings suggest that three young French climbers, members of the Military High Mountain Group from Chamonix, celebrated their organization’s 50th anniversary with a latest route on Peak 41.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that several small teams are attempting difficult climbs on Nepal’s 6,000 and 7,000m peaks. Unfortunately, they rarely report on their intends or progress until they return, and often only if they succeed.

This is what we know about the ongoing expeditions:.

Recent findings suggest that three young French climbers, members of the Military High Mountain Group from Chamonix, celebrated their organization’s 50th anniversary with a latest route on Peak 41. This 6,654m mountain is located in the Khumbu region and is often called the “true Mera Peak.”.

Konrad Piontek, Amaury Fouillade, and Clovis Paulin took advantage of a good weather window and achieved the first ascent of the peak’s northeast face. They climbed in an alpine-style single push over four days. The result is a beautiful 1,400m line with difficulties up to ED+ 5+ M6 A1 90°. They descended via the southeast face. The team named their line Bon Matin (good morning).

It has been revealed that nivel Meroi and Romano Benet are acclimatized and ready to attempt a new route on Jugal II, but the Italian couple will be on their own. Tine Cuder of Slovenia, the third team member, has left due to illness.

Meanwhile, in the Kangchenjunga region, a large Russian team has also finished acclimatizing. The team trekked in the area and crossed a number of high-altitude passes, the latest of them at the top of an icefall at 5,750m. They reported lots of snow above 5,000m but are ready to attempt a new route on the formidable Jannu (7,710m) from its southeast side.

The team comprises Ivan Artemov, Ivan Volkov, Artem Zhdanov, Konstantin Neumoin, Roman Shilin, and Vasily Yagodin.

Hidesuke Taneishi and Tetsu Hashimoto of Japan traveled to Nepal in September, aiming to achieve the first ascent of Gangapurna West (7,455m), also known as Asapurna or Peak Lachenal. They have provided no news since, but they probably had to retreat when an intense snowstorm hit the Annapurna region three weeks ago.

It has been revealed that location of Gangapurna West on a Google Earth screenshot. Notes by Lindsay Griffin for the American Alpine Journal.

Industry observers note that meanwhile, a second team has reached the base of the peak with the same objective. Valery Shamalo, Natalia Zanina, Maksim Trufanov, and Ruslan Kirichenko arrived at the beginning of October and saw no one else there. They reported that recent precipitation had left the trail in a poor state; the climbers had to cross landslides and swollen rivers to reach base camp.

The team has completed two acclimatization climbs, looking for a passage through the icefall at the base of the mountain and then a series of couloirs. They reached 5,900m and, on a second trip, 6,600m. Deep snow covered the peak, which slowed progress. Finally, they launched a summit bid last week.

From 6,600m, they spent a day on technical ice sections of 70–80º. In poor visibility, they endured spindrift and were showered by small ice chunks.

Recent findings suggest that “In the afternoon, the weather deteriorated sharply,” Natalia Zanina stated. “Heavy snowfall began, and we started being struck by large, continuous avalanches. At 6,800m (340m from the summit), we decided to turn back.”.

A note on names: according to 8000ers.com, Asapurna should be the correct name for this peak because — although it is closer to Gangapurna — Asapurna’s summit ridge connects directly to Annapurna III.

The list of climbing permits granted by Nepal’s Ministry of Tourism points to some other interesting expeditions, some of them in remote western Nepal. There is a permit for Nyalu Kang (6,265m), only opened to foreign climbers in 2024 and reportedly unclimbed, and Ardang, summited once by Canadians Bryce Kendall and Sunny Twelker in 2019. Victor Saunders and Mick Fowler of the UK attempted Ardang last year.

Latest Update: Monarch Money Review – Every Household Account in One Shared App, for $99.99 a Year

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1289 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Moneycrashers

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Pay for Monarch Money if you want your household’s budget, bills, investments, and net worth in one app you and a partner both use, since a partner joins the $99.99-a-year Core proposal free.
  • Monarch Money’s CEO, Val Agostino, was among the first product managers at Mint, the free budgeting app Intuit later shut down.
  • Sources indicate that monarch sells two aims, Core and Plus.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Pay for Monarch Money if you want your household’s budget, bills, investments, and net worth in one app you and a partner both use, since a partner joins the $99.99-a-year Core proposal free. Skip Plus, at $199.99, unless you’ll use its retirement forecasts or track a side business.

Monarch Money’s CEO, Val Agostino, was among the first product managers at Mint, the free budgeting app Intuit later shut down. He started the tech giant in 2019 alongside Ozzie Osman and Jon Sutherland. The company now calls its app simply Monarch, and by October 2026 it had more than 1 million members. The app holds 4.9 stars from about 119,000 ratings on Apple’s App Store and 4.8 stars from about 26,000 reviews on Google Play.

Sources indicate that monarch sells two aims, Core and Plus. Everything in this section comes with Core, and the pricing section below covers what Plus adds.

Industry observers note that monarch offers two ways to budget, and you can switch between them. Flex budgeting, the default, sorts expenses into fixed, flexible, and non-monthly groups and has you watch one number, the flexible spending you have left this month. Category budgeting sets a limit for each category, such as groceries or dining out. Either way, Monarch drafts your first budget from your last six months of spending.

It builds each month’s budget on the income you expect, while YNAB has you budget only money that has already arrived. Leftover money in a category can roll over to the next month, which is how Monarch handles once-a-year bills, and alerts warn you before you overspend.

Transactions arrive already sorted into categories, and rules let you correct what the sorting gets wrong. As transactions come in, a rule can match on the merchant, amount, category, or account, then rename the merchant, change the category, add tags, split the charge, or hide it from your budget. The Recurring page finds bills and subscriptions in your history and reveals them as a calendar or a list, with reminders before each charge.

Monarch tracks each investment you hold, not just account balances, across stocks, mutual funds, exchange-traded funds, 401(k)s, and crypto. It highlights how your portfolio splits among stocks, bonds, cash, and other assets and how it has done against the S&P 500. It can also track equity compensation, the stock or options your employer pays you.

Net worth, what you own minus what you owe, refreshes as your linked balances and market prices change. A home’s value can come from Zillow’s estimate and a car’s from VinAudit, crypto can link straight from Coinbase, and anything else goes in as a manual account. U.S. members can add a VantageScore 3.0 credit score from Equifax, which updates monthly and doesn’t affect your credit.

Sources indicate that A save-up goal tells you whether you’re on track from your balance, your target date, and what you strategy to add each month. A pay-down goal projects a payoff date for each debt, and its calculator compares the avalanche method, which pays the highest interest rate first, with the snowball method, which pays the smallest balance first. Goals sit inside the budget, so you see what goes to them each month.

Adding a partner costs nothing, and each person gets a separate login under the one subscription. Every member sees every linked account and transaction, though, and Monarch’s help center says accounts and transactions can’t be hidden from one another. You can mark each as shared or as one person’s to filter transactions, reports, and accounts, but the household keeps one budget.

If you pay for your own subscription, you can also give a financial planner a year of access at no extra cost and revoke it anytime. The planner can view and edit what you see but can’t link accounts for you. A planner in Monarch’s professional program can instead pay for your subscription, at $14.99 a month per client.

Reports cover spending, income, and cash flow, and you can filter them by category, merchant, account, tag, or owner and save the views you use. The Sankey report draws your money flowing from income into each spending category, and a weekly recap sums up spending, cash flow, and net worth.

In a recent development, the AI Assistant, available to U.S. members, answers plain-English questions about your own accounts, such as why spending jumped last month, and explains how to use Monarch. Since November 2026, a test version also looks for savings on its own, such as a duplicate subscription charge. You can hide the AI features in settings, but automatic categorization stays on.

Monarch links to more than 13,000 banks and other institutions through three data providers, Plaid, MX, and Finicity, and suggests the one with the strongest connection history for each bank. Since September 2026, you can switch an institution to another provider without losing its history, and a public status page indicates each provider’s connection record at popular banks. Monarch’s help center states connection problems nearly always lie between the provider and your bank, and that store-brand credit cards and mortgages are harder to keep connected.

According to recent reports, access is read-only, so Monarch can’t move money, and your bank logins go to the data provider, never to Monarch. Data is encrypted in storage and in transit, sign-ins can require two-factor authentication, and independent auditors have certified Monarch under SOC 2, an outside audit of how a company protects customer data.

Recent findings suggest that plus costs $100 more a year and adds four things. Forecasting models your net worth and cash flow decades ahead and tests events like retiring at 55, buying a home, or having a child, with every assumption adjustable. Business tracking keeps an LLC, rental property, or side business apart from your personal money, with a profit-and-loss report for each and tax-prep exports, but no invoicing or payroll. Advanced investment analysis compares holdings with what you paid and breaks funds down by asset class using Morningstar data. Plus also includes a couple’s will from Trust & Will, which Monarch values at $299, once your trial ends.

Plus is worth the extra $100 only if you’ll use the retirement forecasts or track a business in it.

Monarch Money is the budgeting app to pay for when a household wants its budget, bills, investments, and net worth together in one app that two people can share. Its strongest case is a couple who keep some accounts separate but want one view of all of them, especially when one partner invests and wants holdings tracked beside the budget. For most of them, Core at $99.99 a year is all they need to buy.

It’s the wrong pick for anyone who wants spending tracked free, and YNAB suits budgeters who want to blueprint only money already in their accounts. Partners who want any account kept private should look elsewhere too. Everyone else should start the 7-day trial on Monarch’s website, not in an app store, so the WELCOME code and the money-back guarantee both apply. Link every account your household has during the trial, then pay for the year with the code to take 30% off.
